measures.units: Hz, smooth pursuit cutoff frequency (maximum velocity)
measures.evidence_text: Results consistent with earlier finding that 'marijuana does not reduce the maximum velocity of smooth pursuit eye movements'; pre-dose cutoff 1.71 Hz, post-dose ~1.51 to 1.76 Hz (Table XII).

studies.authors: Kleinloog D, Liem-Moolenaar M, Jacobs G, Klaassen E, de Kam M, Hijman R, van Gerven J
studies.title: Does olanzapine inhibit the psychomimetic effects of Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinol?
studies.design: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 5-way crossover interaction trial (THC alone, placebo, olanzapine, THC+olanzapine, THC+diphenhydramine); washout >= 2 weeks
studies.population: healthy male mild cannabis users aged 18-45 (use <= ~once/week in past year); 49 included, 33 completed all 5 days
studies.condition: intrapulmonary (Volcano vaporizer) purified THC 2, 4 and 6 mg at 90-min intervals vs placebo; eye movements measured repeatedly over the day incl. two baselines; values are least-squares means over the session
studies.device: EOG (electrodes on forehead and lateral canthi); saccade stimulus ~15 deg, smooth pursuit sinusoid 0.3-1.1 Hz, 22.5 deg amplitude

measures.units: smooth pursuit, % of time eyes track target (CHDR metric, not gain)
measures.p_or_stat: THC alone vs placebo -2.4% (95% CI -6.1, +1.3), p = 0.208
measures.evidence_text: Table 1 LS means smooth pursuit: THC alone 45.7%, placebo 48.1%; Table 2 THC alone vs placebo -2.4 (-6.1 to +1.3), p = 0.208.
Saccadic peak velocity LS means THC alone 481 vs placebo 480 deg/s; contrast +1 (-11 to +13), p = 0.884.
Saccadic reaction time LS means THC alone 207 vs placebo 200 ms; contrast +6 (-2 to +14), p = 0.111.

measures.units: % saccadic inaccuracy (abs. error as % of target amplitude)
measures.evidence_text: 'thc alone increased saccadic inaccuracy by 0.7% (95%ci 0.1-1.3%; p = 0.033) compared to placebo'; LS means 7.1% vs 6.4%.
Pupil/iris ratio: placebo LS mean 0.55; THC alone vs placebo -0.01 (-0.02 to +0.01), p = 0.558.

studies.authors: Liem-Moolenaar M, te Beek ET, de Kam ML, Franson KL, Kahn RS, Hijman R, Touw D, van Gerven JMA
studies.title: Central nervous system effects of haloperidol on THC in healthy male volunteers
studies.design: double-blind, placebo-controlled, partial 3-way crossover, ascending-dose study
studies.population: healthy male mild cannabis users
studies.condition: ascending intrapulmonary THC doses (dose not stated in available abstract) vs placebo, with/without haloperidol

measures.units: smooth pursuit (% time in pursuit, per trial registry outcome definition)
measures.evidence_text: Abstract: THC vs placebo reduced smooth pursuit (along with alertness, Stroop, word recall, prolactin); haloperidol reduced saccadic peak velocity and smooth pursuit. Registry (NTR1731): 'THC significantly decreased smooth pursuit.'

studies.authors: Marcotte TD, Umlauf A, Grelotti DJ, et al.
studies.title: Evaluation of Field Sobriety Tests for Identifying Drivers Under the Influence of Cannabis: A Randomized Clinical Trial
studies.design: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group clinical trial (NCT02849587)
studies.population: adults 21-55 who used cannabis >= 4 times in past month (mean 16.7 days/30); placebo n = 63, THC n = 121
studies.condition: smoked cannabis ad libitum: placebo 0.02% THC vs 5.9% or 13.4% THC (THC arms combined); FSTs by DRE instructors at median 1 h 10 min (primary 70 min), 2 h 20 min, 3 h 10 min, 4 h 10 min
studies.device: officer-administered field sobriety tests; pupil measurement method not described; HGN NOT assessed

measures.units: % participants whose eyes do not converge (Lack of Convergence test); placebo group vs THC group
measures.evidence_text: Table 2 Eyes do not converge: placebo 31 (49.2%) vs THC 83 (68.6%); OR 2.25 (1.21-4.21), P = .01.

measures.units: mm, MEDIAN (IQR placebo 4.0-6.0; THC 4.5-6.0), between groups
measures.evidence_text: Table 2 Pupillary diameter, median (IQR), mm: placebo 5.0 (4.0-6.0) vs THC 5.5 (4.5-6.0); OR 1.31 (0.99-1.74), P = .06.

measures.units: % with eyelid tremors during Modified Romberg; placebo vs THC group
measures.evidence_text: Eyelid tremors (Modified Romberg): placebo 50 (79.4%) vs THC 96 (79.3%); Finger to Nose eyelid tremor 45 (71.4%) vs 91 (75.2%), OR 1.21 (0.61-2.41), P = .58.

studies.authors: Bosker WM, Theunissen EL, Conen S, et al.
studies.title: A placebo-controlled study to assess Standardized Field Sobriety Tests performance during alcohol and cannabis intoxication in heavy cannabis users and accuracy of point of collection testing devices for detecting THC in oral fluid
studies.design: double-blind, placebo-controlled, three-way design (THC + alcohol placebo, THC + 0.5 mg/mL, THC + 0.7 mg/mL alcohol); baseline SFST on separate drug-free day
studies.population: heavy cannabis users (15 M, 5 F), mean age 24.3
studies.condition: smoked THC 400 µg/kg over 15 min; SFST ~2 h after smoking
studies.device: Standardized Field Sobriety Tests (HGN by trained raters)

measures.units: % participants impaired on HGN (drug-free baseline vs THC alone)
measures.p_or_stat: chi2 = 3.399, df = 1, p = 0.065 (trend); THC+alcohol chi2 = 7.110, df = 2, p = 0.029
measures.evidence_text: 'THC also increased percentage of individuals showing impairment on HGN from 0 to 15 %' (trend); HGN showed no impairment at baseline.

studies.authors: Stough C, Boorman M, Ogden E, Papafotiou K
studies.title: An evaluation of the Standardised Field Sobriety Tests for the detection of impairment associated with cannabis with and without alcohol
studies.journal: NDLERF Monograph Series No. 17 (National Drug Law Enforcement Research Fund, Australia)
studies.design: placebo-controlled repeated-measures (six drug conditions per participant); report
studies.population: two groups of 40 adults with prior cannabis use
studies.condition: smoked THC 0%, 1.8% or 3% cigarettes, with alcohol placebo, 0.03% or 0.05% BAC
studies.device: Standardised Field Sobriety Tests (HGN signs: lack of smooth pursuit, nystagmus at max deviation, onset at 45 deg, head movements/jerks)

measures.evidence_text: Executive summary: 'the percentage of individuals exhibiting each sign of the HGN test increased with the administration of low THC and high THC' vs placebo; head movements/jerks exhibited in a high percentage. Values only in Figures 55-60 (not readable in text).

studies.authors: Hosko MJ, Kochar MS, Wang RIH
studies.title: Effects of orally administered delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol in man
studies.volume_pages: 14(3) (pages not visible in available copy; year inferred from received Sept 1972/accepted Dec 1972)
studies.design: single-blind, placebo-controlled (2 drug nights, 5 placebo nights per subject)
studies.population: healthy males aged 24-28, mixed cannabis experience (none to heavy)
studies.condition: oral THC 200 and 300 µg/kg (one subject 400 µg/kg)

measures.evidence_text: 'No nystagmus was detected in any of the subjects after THC administration.'
'No consistent alteration of respiratory rate or pupil size was noted.'; conjunctival congestion in all subjects at both doses.
